    type: default
    sort: "date desc"
    fields: [title, description, date, reading-time]
    sort-ui: false
    filter-ui: false

  # The rough tier: one-line rows (title + date), no descriptions. Notes are
  # comment-sized — paper reactions, small results, dead ends. Deliberately NOT
  # branded a "second brain": a folder that accumulates when something is worth
  # writing never looks stale; a system that promises upkeep does.
  - id: notes
    contents: notes
    type: default
    sort: "date desc"
    fields: [title, date]
    sort-ui: false
    filter-ui: false

```{=html}
<!-- The staircase hero, with a Now paragraph (2026-08-16). The tricolon
     headline steps rightward — three beats, three indents — set low in the
     frame; the Now paragraph sits directly under it, the one block of prose
     here and the one meant to be rewritten by hand as the work moves. Corners
     carry semantic jobs: identity top-right (role line + links), status alone
     bottom-left, the ledger alone bottom-right. DOM order stays headline →
     role → now → filing (the reading order); the identity corner's position is
     visual only (flex `order`). Each .rise-mask/.rise pair is one beat of the
     entrance choreography (assets/site/hero-motion.html).

     The 2026-08-16 build first tried a fuller "CV first screen" — a selected-
     work strip and a figure plate (a head of the induction post's model reading
     the headline, real baked attention) — and Ameya cut both the same day: the
     strip only repeated the Writing list below, and the plate meant nothing
     outside the induction post. The plate is BANKED for a "latest work" role:
     tools/hero-plate/compute.py + assets/site/hero-plate.html stay in the tree
     unwired; the markup, CSS and _quarto.yml wiring are in commit 84641f7. -->
<section class="hero-screen">
  <div class="hero" aria-labelledby="hero-headline">
    <div class="hero-inner">
      <p id="hero-headline" class="hero-headline" role="heading" aria-level="1"><span class="rise-mask"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 0ms">LLM circuitry&nbsp;—</span></span><span class="rise-mask hl-step-2"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 80ms">implemented, documented,</span></span><span class="rise-mask hl-step-3"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 160ms">shown&nbsp;off.</span></span></p>
      <div class="hero-ident">
        <p class="hero-role"><span class="rise-mask"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 260ms">CS, physics &amp; AI at Penn State.<br>Independent interpretability research.</span></span></p>
        <div class="rise-mask"><nav class="hero-links rise" style="--beat: 320ms" aria-label="Profile links">
          <a href="about/">About</a>
          <a href="https://github.com/Ameya-bit">GitHub</a>
          <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/ameya-bit">LinkedIn</a>
          <a href="mailto:ameyapanchal011@gmail.com">Email</a>
          <a href="resume/">Résumé</a>
        </nav></div>
      </div>

      <!-- Now (2026-08-16): the one paragraph of prose in the hero, first person,
           rewritten by hand as the work moves. Under the headline, in the low
           position the headline holds — the status line beneath it stays the
           machine-checked freshness claim. -->
      <div class="rise-mask"><div class="rise hero-now" style="--beat: 380ms">
        <p class="hero-kicker" role="heading" aria-level="2">Now</p>
        <p>I am in the process of publishing a neutron-star paper, and am transitioning into AI safety research in mechanistic interpretability. Currently I am working to reproduce the early-layer degradation result from the Global Workspace paper (Gurnee et al., 2026).</p>
      </div></div>

      <div class="hero-foot">
        <!-- The status line, genuinely live (2026-08-04). The QUESTION is
             editorial and stays in the markup — it is the one sentence that
             says what I am doing right now. What JS adds is the evidence that
             it is still happening: the last push to the experiment's repo, as
             a relative stamp (assets/site/hero-status.html). Named by
             `data-repo`, so pointing the line at the next project is a
             one-attribute edit.
             The COMMIT MESSAGE is deliberately not shown — "fix seed" in a
             hero is worse than nothing; freshness is the only part of a commit
             stream a visitor can use.
             Both the stamp and the cursor ship `hidden`. The cursor's whole
             claim is "this line is live", so it may only appear once something
             live has actually landed — with JS off, rate-limited, or the repo
             gone, the line renders as the plain question it always was, and
             nothing blinks to promise otherwise. -->
        <p class="hero-status"><span class="rise-mask"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 440ms">Current experiment&ensp;·&ensp;Does Anthropic's global workspace result replicate?<span class="hero-pulse" data-repo="Ameya-bit/jacobian-lens-from-scratch" hidden></span><span class="hero-cursor" aria-hidden="true" hidden></span></span></span></p>
        <!-- The ledger (the banked catalogue-cover move, adopted 2026-08-04): the
             hero's bottom-right corner is the site's table of contents — one row
             per collection, trailing mono numerals for the honest counts (mono is
             the numbering system, nothing else). The hardcoded counts are correct
             at publish time; the script at the foot of this file re-reads them
             from the rendered listings so they can never drift.

             INSTRUMENTS (2026-08-06) is the first row that leaves this page, and
             the first whose count the script cannot check: /instruments/ is a
             hand-written page, not a Quarto listing, so there is nothing on the
             homepage to count. It therefore carries no `data-counts` and the
             script skips it by construction rather than by accident. The rows on
             that page are the source of truth — add one there, change the 05
             here. -->
        <nav class="hero-ledger" aria-label="Site contents"><span class="rise-mask"><span class="rise" style="--beat: 500ms">
          <a href="#writing-section" data-counts="writing">Writing<span class="ledger-n">03</span></a>
          <a href="#notes-section" data-counts="notes">Notes<span class="ledger-n">03</span></a>
          <a href="instruments/">Instruments<span class="ledger-n">05</span></a>
        </span></span></nav>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
<!-- Panda engine disabled 2026-08-03: the minimalist base gets finished first,
     whimsy returns only once the base stands on its own (design/direction.md,
     session log). Assets and engine stay in assets/pandas/; development

     `#panda-stage` div above and the loader script from git history. -->
```

<!-- Kickers are p+role=heading, not h2: the section-numeral machinery is
     scoped to main.content h2s and would stamp a gutter "01" on these labels
     (same reason the hero headline is a p). Visible on BOTH lists (2026-08-04,
     Ameya's catch): the label used to live only in the hero's cue, which the
     seam dims on scroll — so by the time the reader reached the list, its
     name had faded out. Labels belong to the content they label. -->
<p class="list-kicker" role="heading" aria-level="2">Writing</p>

```{=html}
<!-- The colophon whisper (2026-08-06). /colophon/ is deliberately NOT a ledger
     row: the ledger files work, and a page about how the site is built is the
     site talking about itself. A quiet centred line under everything is the rank
     that claim deserves — and it is the exact object this rule was written for
     back when it carried a panda credit. -->
<p class="site-colophon"><a href="colophon/">Colophon</a> — how this site is built.</p>
```

```{=html}
<!-- The ledger's honest-count guarantee: re-read each collection's size from
     the listings this same page just rendered. No fetch, no state — if JS is
     off, the publish-time numbers in the markup stand (and were true when
     written). padStart keeps the two-digit filing format the numerals share
     with the posts' section counters. -->
<script>
  document.querySelectorAll(".hero-ledger a[data-counts]").forEach(function (a) {
    var n = document.querySelectorAll("#listing-" + a.getAttribute("data-counts") + " .quarto-post").length;
    var el = a.querySelector(".ledger-n");
    if (el && n) el.textContent = String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  });
</script>
```
